title: slash-restart-saves-the-slate-then-hands-off
author: cc
what: A `/restart` skill CC fires on itself: it measures what is behind this session, closes the boundary the way a boundary is closed (a slate through the saveslate door), and then hands off -- either by asking the inner loop to bring this session back, or by standing a new instance up beside it. One word, and the session is on the new build with its continuity written down.
why: Today the act is three commands a tired operator has to remember in the right order, and the order is the whole safety of it: measure, save, then relaunch. Getting it wrong in the other order is a session that ends with nothing written down. Akien, 2026-09-22: 'cairn restart and cairn cc.x restart and slash restart. We only need to have you around to supervise the process the first time.' The skill is the third name, and it is the one CC types.
how:
Three steps, in this order and no other. (1) `cairn cc restart status` -- the measurement decides the branch: `inner loop: HOLDING (pid N)` means a loop is behind this session and `now` will bring it back; anything else means there is nothing behind it and `spawn` is the only safe verb. (2) Fire /saveslate -- as a skill, not shelled, because its door demands instruments_read.git_heads matching the live repos and only CC can compile that. A refusal here ABORTS: a restart that relaunched anyway would have spent the conversation to save nothing. (3) Fire the verb the measurement chose. On the `spawn` branch nothing dies -- the skill reports the new instance's remote-control name and STOPS; it must not then kill anything.

THE BUILD SPEC IS THE `decisions` LIST ON THIS TICKET: D1..D7, settled 2026-09-22 by CC inside the bounds already cast here, each composed from code that already stands and naming its source. A ticket is a list of one-line decisions and the rehearsal reads that list; prose in `how` is the first cut, the decisions are the build.
traces_to: Law 1 -- the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled: the safe order (measure, save, relaunch) is settled and today has no address but an operator's memory. Also CP4 -- design to the tool: the tool is a CC session that cannot restart itself, and the skill is the one surface that session can reach.
falsifier: GREEN when a session is relaunched by typing one word and the slate written in that act is readable afterward with the pre-restart git heads in its instruments_read. RED if /restart can end a session that has no loop behind it and no spawned replacement already reachable -- a hang-up, the one failure this skill must never cause.

constraints.text: The order is status, then slate, then relaunch -- never slate-then-status. The status decides which relaunch verb is fired, and arming a flag before knowing whether anything can consume it is the hang-up this skill exists to prevent.
A slate refusal aborts the restart. The slate and the relaunch are one act; half of it is worse than none.
Match on HOLDING, and treat every other status output as NONE. The safe branch is the one that kills nothing, so an unparseable status must fall to `spawn`, never to `now`.
/saveslate is FIRED AS A SKILL, never shelled. Its door refuses a packet whose instruments_read.git_heads do not match the live repos, and only a CC session can compile those.
On the spawn branch this session does not end. The skill reports the new instance's remote-control name and stops; killing anything after a successful spawn is out.

This skill relaunches ONE Claude Code process and nothing beneath it. `cairn restart` is the system's restart and does not touch running cc instances (Akien, 2026-09-22); two different acts may not wear one word.

children: none, because the skill is a composition of two things that already exist and are already proved -- cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart and skills/saveslate/ -- so there is no part of it that could prove independently before the whole. The one new artifact is the branch selector, and it is the thing the proof at skills/restart/proofs/ drives.

watchme.trigger: a new file appears under the superclaude flags home's consumed/ folder -- the restart history, written by the inner loop when it consumes a one-shot flag by MOVING it. The probe fires on the beat that already runs; no poller.
watchme.enough: three consecutive restarts each of which has a slate in CairnCommons/slates/ written within the minute before its consumed stamp, at which point the probe retires. Any single restart with no slate behind it is carried immediately rather than waiting for the third -- that is the failure the skill exists to prevent.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, naming the consumed flag's stamp and the slate id found (or the explicit absence), so the carry is the pairing rather than a boolean.
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree -- a restart with no slate behind it kills the hypothesis that a skill step is enough to make the save happen, and points at physics (the verb refusing to relaunch without one) instead.
watchme.consumer: whoever fires the next /restart, via the cc device's pane -- a restart that lost its slate is a live trouble, not a log line.

links.what: cairn restart cycles the SYSTEM -- the sibling name. Akien ruled the boundary on 2026-09-22: that one does NOT restart the running cc instance(s); this one is the only thing that touches a CC session.

the dispatcher resolves an instance address -- `cairn cc.1 restart`. The third name. /restart fires `cairn cc restart` on instance 0, so it does not wait on that ticket, but the spawn branch's report reads better once `cairn cc.1 restart` resolves.
the verb this skill composes -- status|now|fresh|onexit|spawn|standdown|clear, landed 2026-09-22 in commits da6f8b01 and 6261e14d.
the door the boundary is closed through -- step 2, and the abort condition.

Once we know it works we don't have to do any of that. ... No, cairn restart does not restart the running cc instance(s). Otherwise yes, approved all the way to proved.

MEASURED, and it decides which branch gets exercised first: every session alive today was launched by a superclaude that still exec'd claude (the loop landed in da6f8b01, after they started), so `cairn cc restart status` reports NONE for all of them and the FIRST firing of /restart takes the spawn branch. The loop branch stays unmeasured until a session launched after that commit fires it -- which is exactly the supervised first run Akien described.

decisions.text: PLACEMENT, AND THE MEASURED HOLDINGS THE OTHER DECISIONS STAND ON (measured 2026-09-22; the reader has no repository, so this paragraph IS the repository for these names). The skill berths at skills/restart/ in class-space, beside the fifteen skills already there (cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, design, idea, intent, moreabout, note, ruled, sail, saveslate, sorted, tellmeabout, whatslefttodo). Four files are written there: SKILL.md (D4), selector.py (D2), proofs/test_restart_selector.py (D3), intention+why.json (D5); one symlink is made outside the repo (D6); one probe is armed at cairn/devices/cc/probes/a_restart_leaves_a_slate_behind_it.py (D7). HOLDINGS: (h1) skills/saveslate/ is the template folder and holds exactly SKILL.md, intention+why.json, door.py, proofs/, probes/, validations/, state.json, history.json. (h2) A SKILL.md opens with a YAML frontmatter block delimited by lines of three hyphens carrying exactly two keys, `name:` and `description:` (one line each), then a level-1 markdown heading and numbered prose sections; skills/saveslate/SKILL.md is the model to copy the shape from. (h3) ~/.claude/skills/ holds one symlink per skill, each pointing at /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/skills/<name> (measured: fifteen such links, e.g. saveslate -> /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/skills/saveslate). (h4) cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart is the verb this skill drives; `cairn cc restart status` prints one `key: value` line per fact and the branch-deciding line is `inner loop: HOLDING (pid <N>)` when a loop holds the session and `inner loop: NONE -- this session cannot relaunch itself` otherwise; the verbs are status|now|fresh|onexit|spawn [N]|standdown|clear. (h5) The superclaude inner loop's flags home is $HOME/.cairn/launchers/superclaude/<instance>/ and it is exported to the session as SUPERCLAUDE_FLAGS_HOME; a consumed one-shot is MOVED to <flags home>/consumed/<flag>.<stamp> where <stamp> is `date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S` (launchers/superclaude:81-82). (h6) A slate is a JSON file at CairnCommons/slates/<id>.json carrying id, date, written_at (ISO, no timezone), session, author, at_sea, next_direction, open_threads. (h7) A Cairn probe module declares a module-level `PROBE` that is a frozen cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe built with keyword arguments why, trigger, to, verb, channel, body, carry, enough, horizon; trigger is `(now, context) -> bool`, carry is `(context) -> dict | None`, enough is `(context) -> bool`; cairn/devices/cc/probes/is_the_memory_curve_recorded.py is the module in exactly that shape to copy. (h8) cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path(device, instance=0, roots=None) -> Path resolves ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>. (h9) cairn.tools.base.probe.owning_ticket(<ticket id or slug>) is what a probe's carry puts in its "ticket" key. (h10) A skill proof is a plain python module run as __main__ (NOT pytest): it inserts the repo root on sys.path, defines an ok(name, cond, detail="") helper that prints and raises SystemExit(1) on a red, defines main() -> int, and ends `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`; skills/saveslate/proofs/test_slate_door.py is the module in exactly that shape. BUILD ORDER: D2 (the selector) then D3 (its proof) then D4 (the prose that calls it) then D5, D6, D7. A decision's number is its address, not its build order.

THE SELECTOR IS CODE, NOT PROSE, AND IT LIVES AT skills/restart/selector.py. It is a module with one public function: `def branch(status_text: str) -> str`. It returns the literal string "now" if and only if the text contains a line whose content, after stripping, begins with "inner loop:" and whose remainder after the colon, stripped, begins with the word HOLDING (compared case-foldedly through cairn.tools.system_word.fold, because HOLDING is a word the system prints and a system word folds). It returns the literal string "spawn" for EVERYTHING else -- no loop line, a loop line saying NONE, an empty string, unparseable bytes, a status command that failed. There is no third return value and no exception path: an unreadable status is not an error to raise, it is the safe branch, because the safe branch is the one that kills nothing (the ticket's third constraint, verbatim: "Match on HOLDING, and treat every other status output as NONE"). The module also carries `HOLDING = "HOLDING"` and `LOOP_LINE_PREFIX = "inner loop:"` as module constants so the proof and the prose name the same strings. The selector is code rather than a sentence in SKILL.md precisely so it can be proved (D3); a branch condition that lives only in prose is a branch nobody can red.

THE PROOF: skills/restart/proofs/test_restart_selector.py, in the plain-module shape of holding (h10). It imports `branch` from the sibling selector module by inserting skills/restart on sys.path (the same way skills/saveslate/proofs/test_slate_door.py inserts skills/saveslate and imports door). Module-level PROVES = {"15b80c0c393c": {"all": "test_only_holding_selects_the_session_ending_verb"}} -- the ticket key a STRING LITERAL, because proof_coverage.declared reads it with ast.literal_eval, and the falsifier is unnumbered so its single clause name is "all". ONE composite tooth of that name, taking no arguments, asserting with bare assert and printing a green line per assertion. The tooth drives branch() over these captured forms and asserts the outcome for each: (a) the full `cairn cc restart status` output of a HELD session, containing the line `inner loop: HOLDING (pid 12345)` among five other lines -> "now"; (b) the full output of an UNHELD session, containing `inner loop: NONE -- this session cannot relaunch itself` -> "spawn"; (c) the empty string -> "spawn"; (d) garbled bytes -- a string with no colon, no newline and non-ascii -- -> "spawn"; (e) a line that MENTIONS holding in another position, e.g. `tmux sessions: cairn_cc_1: 1 windows (HOLDING)` with the loop line saying NONE -> "spawn", which is the tooth a hollow selector written as a bare substring search could not pass; (f) lowercase `inner loop: holding (pid 12345)` -> "now", the system-word fold. Run the proof twice bare before sealing; check the clause names against proof_coverage.clauses before the first seal. FORWARD POINTER, SO THIS STEP IS READABLE ALONE: the five fixture forms this decision names -- HELD, UNHELD, WORD_ELSEWHERE, HELD_LOWER, GARBLED -- are NOT left to the builder to invent. Their exact captured bytes are at D8, transcribed from the live verb. Read D8 before writing the proof; nothing about the fixtures is settled separately from this ticket.

SKILL.md: skills/restart/SKILL.md, in the shape of holding (h2). Frontmatter `name: restart` and a one-line `description:` saying the skill measures what is behind this session, writes the slate, and then hands off. The body is three numbered sections in this order and no other, each naming the exact command or skill it fires: (1) MEASURE -- run `cairn cc restart status`, capture stdout, and hand the captured text to `branch()` from skills/restart/selector.py (`PYTHONPATH=$HOME/dev/src/cairn python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '$HOME/dev/src/cairn/skills/restart'); import selector; print(selector.branch(sys.stdin.read()))"`). The prose states the two outcomes and says the selector, not the reader, decides. (2) SAVE -- fire /saveslate AS A SKILL, through the Skill tool, never shelled: its door refuses a packet whose instruments_read.git_heads do not match the live repos and only a CC session can compile those. If /saveslate refuses -- any refusal, for any reason -- THE SKILL ABORTS HERE: it prints the refusal verbatim, states that nothing was relaunched, and stops. It does not retry, does not fall back, and does not arm a flag. (3) HAND OFF -- fire the verb step 1 chose: `cairn cc restart now` on the "now" branch (this ends the conversation; the loop brings it back), or `cairn cc restart spawn` on the "spawn" branch. On the spawn branch the skill then REPORTS the new instance's tmux session and its remote-control name as printed by the verb, and STOPS -- it must not kill, sign off, or arm any flag afterward; nothing dies on this branch. The file closes with a "Stay honest" section naming the one failure the skill must never cause: ending a session that has no loop behind it and no reachable replacement. FORWARD POINTER, SO THIS STEP IS READABLE ALONE: the two pieces this decision leaves unspelled -- HOW SKILL.md fires /saveslate, and the exact content of the closing 'Stay honest' section -- are at D9, in full. Read D9 before writing SKILL.md; neither is settled separately from this ticket.

THE SYMLINK, AND IT IS A SYMLINK, NOT A COPY: `ln -s /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/skills/restart /home/akien/.claude/skills/restart`, matching holding (h3) -- fifteen existing skills reach the client exactly this way, and a copy would be a second authority that drifts. The link is made in the same act as the skill files, and it is the whole of "the skill is reachable": there is no registration step, no manifest, and no restart of the client needed. This link lives outside both repos (it is in ~/.claude, which is instance-space) so it is NOT committed and NOT in git; it is re-made by hand on a fresh box, and that is a named edge rather than a gap -- the other fifteen have the same property.

THE WATCHME PROBE: cairn/devices/cc/probes/a_restart_leaves_a_slate_behind_it.py, a module in the shape of holding (h7), copying cairn/devices/cc/probes/is_the_memory_curve_recorded.py. It reads two folders and pairs them. CONSUMED = the flags home's consumed folder: for each instance folder under Path.home()/".cairn"/"launchers"/"superclaude", the subfolder "consumed"; every file there is named <flag>.<stamp> with <stamp> in %Y%m%dT%H%M%S local time (holding h5). SLATES = /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/slates/*.json, each carrying `written_at` as an ISO timestamp with no timezone (holding h6). TRIGGER: a consumed file whose stamp is NEWER than the stamp the probe last carried -- the probe keeps that watermark in instance-space at instance_path("cc", 0) / "probes" / "a_restart_leaves_a_slate_behind_it.json" (holding h8), and an absent watermark file means every consumed file is new. It reads those folders on the beat the ground loop already runs: NO poller, and the skill pokes nothing. CARRY: the PAIRING, never a boolean -- {"ticket": owning_ticket("15b80c0c393c"), "consumed": "<flag>.<stamp>", "consumed_at": "<iso>", "slate": "<slate id>" | None, "slate_written_at": "<iso>" | None, "paired": true|false} where a slate pairs with a consumed flag iff its written_at falls in the sixty seconds BEFORE the consumed stamp. An unpaired restart is carried IMMEDIATELY on the beat it is seen -- it is the failure the skill exists to prevent, and it does not wait for a third sample. ENOUGH: three consecutive consumed flags, in stamp order, each paired; at that point the probe retires. The probe carries NO AUTHORITY: it deposits and pokes, and the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act (Law 6). It must be armed BEFORE the WATCHME crossing -- the emission gate resolves ARMED from the path this ticket's watchme.probe field names and refuses an unarmed one. AND THE MODULE IS SPELLED HERE WHOLE, so the builder needs no template file open beside them (the gap both rehearsal passes named, twice each). The imports are exactly: `from __future__ import annotations`, then `json`, then `from datetime import datetime`, `from pathlib import Path`, then `from cairn.tools.base import address` and `from cairn.tools.base.probe import Probe, owning_ticket`. The module defines four module-level callables -- `_consumed()` returning the list of consumed-file names newest-last, `_trigger(now, context) -> bool`, `_carry(context) -> dict`, `_enough(context) -> bool` -- and then ONE frozen module-level `PROBE`. `cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe` is a frozen dataclass with exactly ten fields and these are their values here, every one passed BY KEYWORD: `why=` one sentence saying a restart that leaves no slate behind it is the failure this skill exists to prevent, and a probe that never fires gathers nothing while looking like learning; `trigger=_trigger`; `to="harbor_master"` (the same address is_the_memory_curve_recorded.py pokes -- the deposit lane, not a device that would have to act); `verb=""` (the field's own default: the poke carries no verb, the body says what it is); `channel="personal"` (the default -- the inbox where a device is reached); `body={"nexus": "hypothesize", "kind": "efficacy"}` (the STATIC part, known at declaration: this is an efficacy watch and the hypothesize tree is what it teaches, matching this ticket's watchme.nexus); `carry=_carry`; `while_true=False` (the default, and the right one: poke once at the crossing, never on every pulse the condition holds); `enough=_enough`; `horizon=100` (pulses, not seconds -- how many beats this watch may stand having never fired before its own silence is a finding; 100 is the value the cc device's other probe declares). The module closes with an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block printing `json.dumps({...}, indent=2)` over the consumed count, `_trigger(None, {})` and `_enough({})`, so the probe can be run by hand to see what it would say. Field order in the dataclass is `why, trigger, to, verb, channel, body, carry, while_true, enough, horizon`; `trigger` takes `(now, context)` and `carry`/`enough` take `(context)` alone. FORWARD POINTER, SO THIS STEP IS READABLE ALONE: the three pieces this decision leaves unspelled -- the watermark file's JSON shape, what the if-__main__ block prints, and the algorithm of each of the four module-level callables -- are at D11, in full. Read D11 before writing the probe; none of them is settled separately from this ticket.

D3's FIXTURES ARE CAPTURED HERE VERBATIM, so the builder pastes them rather than constructing realistic-looking ones. cmd_status (cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart:100-121) prints, in order: 'instance flags home: <path or the literal <unset -- launched without the restart loop>>'; then EITHER 'inner loop:          HOLDING (pid <N>)' followed by 'claude under it:     pid <N>' (or 'claude under it:     none found'), OR 'inner loop:          NONE -- this session cannot relaunch itself' and NO claude-under-it line at all; then 'claude on disk:      <version or ?>'; then, ONLY when the flags home is set and exists, 'standing signals:   <flags or two spaces then none>' and 'restarts on record:  <n>'; then always 'tmux sessions:       <tmux ls, newlines squeezed to spaces, or the literal no tmux server>'. The label column is padded to 21 characters, so the loop line's remainder starts at column 22. The proof's fixtures are therefore: HELD = the seven lines 'instance flags home: /home/akien/.cairn/launchers/superclaude/0', 'inner loop:          HOLDING (pid 12345)', 'claude under it:     pid 12346', 'claude on disk:      1.2.3', 'standing signals:     none', 'restarts on record:  4', 'tmux sessions:       cairn_cc_1: 1 windows'. UNHELD = the four lines 'instance flags home: <unset -- launched without the restart loop>', 'inner loop:          NONE -- this session cannot relaunch itself', 'claude on disk:      1.2.3', 'tmux sessions:       no tmux server' -- note it is FOUR lines, not six: the claude-under-it line and the two flag lines are absent on the unheld branch, and a fixture that carried them would not be a real unheld status. WORD_ELSEWHERE = a NONE loop line plus 'tmux sessions:       cairn_cc_1: 1 windows (HOLDING)'. HELD_LOWER = 'inner loop:          holding (pid 12345)'. GARBLED = one line of lone surrogates and a snowman, no colon and no newline. MEASURED: the proof is green twice bare and the named hollow build reds at the WORD_ELSEWHERE clause.

D4's TWO UNSPECIFIED PIECES, SETTLED. (1) HOW SKILL.md FIRES /saveslate: as a SKILL, through the Skill tool -- the SKILL.md line is 'Fire /saveslate as a skill, through the Skill tool. Never shell it', and the reason is spelled beside it: the saveslate door refuses a packet whose instruments_read.git_heads do not match the live repos, and only a CC session can compile those. There is NO command form and no API call; naming one would be the defect. SUCCESS vs REFUSAL: any refusal, for any reason, ABORTS the restart -- SKILL.md says print the refusal verbatim, state that nothing was relaunched, and stop; do not retry, do not fall back to a shorter slate, and do not arm a flag. The why rides with it: the slate and the relaunch are one act, and half of it is worse than none, because a session spent with nothing written down is the failure the slate exists to prevent (Law 7). (2) THE 'Stay honest' SECTION: it is not copied from saveslate, it is written to this skill's own one-sentence rule -- that the failure this skill must never cause is a HANG-UP, a session ended with no loop behind it and no reachable replacement already standing -- then names the three design choices that bend toward it (the asymmetric match, the abort on a slate refusal, the spawn branch that kills nothing), then the tie-breaker 'if any step is ambiguous, the answer is spawn', then the two lines every skill closes on: report a skipped step as skipped, and 'Restarted' is verified by the new session existing, never by this one's narration.

D5's THREE OPEN POINTS, SETTLED, and the file is written. (1) The 'what' paragraph is the builder's to write and D5 states its RULES rather than its bytes, which is the right shape for a charter field: it must name the three steps in order, name selector.py as the thing that decides the branch, give both words it can return and the condition for each, and say why the branch is code rather than prose. As written it does exactly that. (2) filed_edges IS A JSON ARRAY OF TWO STRINGS, each one sentence, each opening with the word UNMEASURED: that 'claude --continue' restores enough of the conversation for a relaunched session to pick the work up, and that 'cairn cc restart status' is fresh enough to act on (it reads a pid file and a live process, and both can change between the read and the relaunch). traces_to is likewise a JSON array, two strings, Law 1 and Law 7 with the sentence of each. (3) claim_provenance's 'cc-read' values are LITERAL, not placeholders -- the same three keys with the same three values stand in skills/saveslate/intention+why.json, and the token means the claim was read by CC rather than measured by an instrument. input_contract is the empty object, literally {}: this skill takes no packet, it is prose plus a selector, not a door.

D7's LAST THREE UNSPECIFIED PIECES, SETTLED, and the probe is armed. (1) THE WATERMARK FILE IS JSON, one key: {"watermark": "<the consumed file's NAME, verbatim>"} and nothing else. It stores the NAME, not a parsed timestamp, because the name is what was read off disk and a re-parse of it is reproducible while a re-formatted timestamp is a second representation to keep in step.
